searchText: Am I correct in understanding that the first slashed validator (20075) did not get an additional penalty during the halfway point? (I assumed 15 slashings of 32 ETH, not sure of the exact value but it's approximately that) Perhaps someone here has a clue who is the pool/person that is being slashed on each proposal, but the addresses used for the deposit have several hundred validators coming in still. It would be great if someone with some social network visibility shouts to turn these validators offline <@!399309815517544451> has been in contact with the slashed provider and they are aware of the issue idk why they aren't stopping though.. Any news on the root cause? Is it a beacon node issue? Not a client issue or a beacon node issue, they were running multiple copies of the same keys due to a bug in their (custom) infrastructure. I don’t know more than that That's fine, just wanted to know if there was going to be a pre-Christmas panic update to software. Let's start betting on the underlying issue: my guess, they tested only on pyrmont where proposing is not that easy, as most slashings were for proposal violations At this time of year it's a very binary "does this require me to fix something?" question. As the answer is a "no" I'm happy 🎄 same here 😅 Does anyone know who runs the EthStaker Discord server or why they want me to do KYC in order to participate in the server? <@!97774605351010304> ^^ kyc? should be a google captcha but yes, scams/bots It doesn't stop scams/bots. it actually does stop 95%+ of them.. Also, it requires I give the bot a list of all Discord servers I'm in, along with my Discord identifying information. It doesn't stop the bots that you care about. 🙂 It stops people from spamming (inside) the Discord server, but doesn't stop them from DM spamming/scamming your users. Crypto discord servers tend to have relatively little problems with raids (spamming inside the server) and a huge problem with DM scams. If it didn't ask for a list of every Discord server I'm in I wouldn't care much, but I'm not a fan of giving that info out. I don't want people knowing I'm part of Black Hats R Us Discord server. 😉 they need to bypass the captcha in order to get the user data. It does not 100% stop them, but a lot of them. we had the "kyc" bot offline for a week Only once, ever. and got a lot of scam reports if you have a better solution let me know i can also set the "kyc" bot to have a requirement of X reddit Karma There isn't one. 🙂 I mod several servers with scammer/spammer problems and we are all basically at the point of giving up. i can make it harder but going to keep it friendly as long as the bots don't spam too many users 🙂 The attacker merely needs to join the server with a legitimate account, go through captcha, and then harvest the user list. They can then use that user list to scam/spam all of the users of your server. sure, that's quite a bit of work. Discord bans are IP bans. doing nothing < doing something You will never know which account is the mole. You sound like a politician. 😢 This is absolutely wrong in many situations. so what is your suggestion? Just disable it and accept that scammers will DM your users no matter what you do. also not true, the spamming bots need to be in the same server as the user having one legitimate account does not allow you to spam users from a different account At least this way your legitimate users don't have to de-anonymize themselves to join. Your verification process isn't preventing them from joining the server. It just kicks them out after 30 minutes. In most cases, the spammers DM within a second or two of joining. it does not, have you looked into the verification methods? it's only google captcha now, because we don't get any reports. can switch to banning too. The very first step is to login with Discord account. The permissions requested from Discord by the bot for the OAuth is "A list of all servers you are in". > In most cases, the spammers DM within a second or two of joining. unverfied users don't see the verified users => can't dm them You don't have to *see* a user to DM them. You only have to share a server with them. It would be awesome if Discord would make it so you have to share a *channel* with someone to DM them, but unless things have changed recently that isn't the case. This slows the scammers down a bit but doesn't stop the problem, I have banned probably 10,000 scammers at this point. They still show up. 🤷‍♂️ (we have some automated mass ban tools that have allowed us to catch some huge swaths of scammers) Okay good to know. As long as i don't see any/many "scam" reports I don't think a change to this is needed Can you at least change the bot's permission requirements so that it doesn't need user server list? Or is it a third party bot that doesn't let you choose that? Altdentifier is not my bot yea So I'm giving my server list and handle to some rando on the internet. 😢 This is why we can't have nice things. FWIW, while I disagree with your approach here, I don't blame you. The scammer problem is *incredibly* frustrating. Just saving the stakers' money It is just equally frustrating to see people give up privacy for a tiny bit of security. 2 weeks ago @ ethstaker hard to make everyone happy 😓 <@!301186049323958275> Why not use a different Discord account if you're concerned about doxxing yourself? It isn't good opsec to be mixing your black hats r us persona with your work persona regardless 1 account per server, at the extreme The political solution is to *appear to do something* whether it is helpful or not. The harder path to follow is to stay true to the Ethereum ethos of privacy and censorship resistance in the face of people asking for you to do *something* to protect them from the world. Heh, I do for the really divergent stuff. 🙂 None the less, I don't want to dox myself even for my more honest work. 😉 This ends up being a usability nightmare sadly. My *guess* is that there is a subset of scammers who are just script kiddies using some off-the-shelf Discord mass DM spam tool. If your server has *anything* out of the ordinary in place these tools won't work properly. In such a case, a simple "check the box to see the other channels" may do the trick. Maybe I'll try this on one of my servers to see if the DM scams decrease at all. mhm i can just say that there is a significant difference in having / not having the bot. i also manually give users the verified role if i know they are legit so you could have also just dm'd me 🙂 I'd ask how you can tell this is the real Micah, but scrolling back over the past few pages of discourse I can vouch it's _definitely_ him 😉 just went throught the KYC in dm's it's him 🙂
